record.original_question: Given a planar figure, or more generally a body in space, and a distance d > 0, what is the smallest number of points A_1, A_2, ... that can be placed in the region so that every other point A in the region lies within distance d of at least one chosen point?

evidence.quote: What is the minimum number of points {A1, A2, ... } included in a given planar figure (generally: in a space body) such that if another point A is included in that figure then there exists at least an Ai with the distance |AAi | < d ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $n=3$) be a bounded region (a planar figure when $n=2$, a body in space when $n=3$), and let $d>0$ be a fixed real number. Define a $d$-covering set of $K$ to be a finite set of points $\{A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N\} \subset K$ such that for every point $A \in K$ there exists some index $i$ with Euclidean distance $|AA_i| < d$. 

Determine, as a function of $K$ and $d$, the minimum cardinality $N(K,d)$ of such a $d$-covering set; equivalently, find the smallest number of open balls of radius $d$ centered at points of $K$ whose union contains $K$. Provide a general method, formula, or sharp bounds for $N(K,d)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the minimum number of points (equivalently, of fixed-radius balls) needed to cover a given planar or spatial region is a classical geometric covering question. While many particular instances (covering a disk by smaller disks, covering a square, etc.) have been studied with partial results and bounds, there is no general closed-form answer for arbitrary planar figures or three-dimensional bodies; it remains an active area in computational and discrete geometry, with exact optimal values known only for special cases.

status_evidence.title: Disk covering problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The disk covering problem asks for the smallest real number r(n) such that n disks of radius r(n) can cover the unit disk. Optimal solutions are known only for small n.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases of the covering problem are solved; the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Covering a disk by disks
status_evidence.snippet: Dumitrescu and Jiang study covering a disk by smaller disks, giving bounds rather than exact answers in general.
status_evidence.claim: General covering numbers are bounded but not exactly determined.

status_evidence.title: On exact covering with unit disks
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work on exact covering with unit disks indicates the problem is still actively researched.
status_evidence.claim: The general covering question is still studied and not closed.
